goal: clear pending items found by scanning the app

sweeps.how: every covered or partial surface's evidence pointer is resolved to a repo script, and the named mode string is looked for in that script
every settings key the settings screens patch, and every AppState field, is looked for as a reader outside the settings screens (optional chaining and the store included)
every exported name in src, electron, scripts, and extensions is looked for as an importer in another file
the parity map's deferred notes and partial limits are read as recorded incompleteness

items.reason: state.connectors had no reader; connectorLines now feeds the request and the section states the count, asserted by local-jobs-check and the surface sweep.
now names the account holder in the request through whoIsThis in src/api.ts, asserted by local-jobs-check.
now travels with the account holder in the request and in the local server's /v1/status payload for the phone page.
a seat count only has meaning on the vendor's account servers, which are deferred; the field stays as the local display of the workspace.
workspace membership is administered by the vendor's servers, deferred with team administration; locally it is a list you keep.
this is a local ledger you record yourself, because billing is a vendor-server feature that is deferred.
the xAI model list now comes from the generated provider catalog, so MODELS was removed; a rescan reports no dead exports.
nothing imported it after the provider layer settled; removed, and the rescan reports no dead exports.
every covered and partial surface now names a repo script and mode, and parity-check.cjs fails when the script or mode is missing.
Uses the web speech engine in the composer and the system voice for replies; the vendor's signed speech helper is deferred.
Links are local to this Mac. Sharing to another account needs the vendor's servers, which is deferred.
Needs the macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility grants; actions are refused until this Mac allows them.
Needs Xcode's simulator tools and a booted device; the pane is empty without them.
A page read needs a site grant accepted in the browser's own permission prompt before it can return text.
Counts tokens seen by this app, not an account meter.
A local ledger you record yourself; no real charge is made.
Local profile fields only; signing in to a vendor account is deferred.
Requires the vendor's own identity backend and OAuth client, which only that vendor can issue; nothing on this Mac can stand in for a hosted sign-in. The app keeps a local account instead.
Teams, seats, roles, and admin policy live on the vendor's servers and are enforced by their account service; a local app has no fleet to administer. Local roles and local shares are the counterpart.
These run on the vendor's cloud while the machine is off, driven by their scheduler servers. The local scheduler covers routines that run on this Mac.
Relayed through the vendor's hosted service, which brokers the connection. The local server already accepts phone handoff and the Chrome companion over 127.0.0.1.
OTel monitoring and retention policies are server-side controls over a hosted fleet; a local app has no server fleet to monitor or retain.
Shipped as a signed vendor binary we do not have or distribute. This app uses the web speech engine in the composer and the system voice for reading replies.
The source product hosts a hosted canvas integration for shared boards. Modbitx artifacts are local documents with a sandboxed preview, so a hosted board has no local server to live on.
Status corrected: the parent's renderer claim was wrong. Partial until a bundled Mermaid renderer ships.

Artifact comments in the source product are shared across accounts on the vendor's server. A local comment store would have no second reader; versions and the compare view cover the local review case.
Printing is reachable through the exported PDF or the local page opened in a browser; a native print dialog is not wired, and this is recorded rather than implied.
Listening can be started and stopped in the composer, and a refused microphone is reported; the engine itself is the browser's, so recognition quality is not ours to test.
The single-turn flow is real and proven; the multi-step loop is roadmap P1, so the limit stands until it ships.
Writing and exporting pptx is real; the preview gap is recorded until a slide-deck preview lands.
The scheduler and Dispatch cover delayed runs; a concurrent-agent panel is roadmap P1, so the limit stands.
Composer dictation works; the global hotkey is a P1 item recorded as the limit.
One system voice reads replies; multi-speaker playback is a P1 item recorded as the limit.
Quick entry and collapse are real; session popouts and sidebar customization are P1, so the limit stands.
Screenshot control is real; the live stream is a P2 item recorded as the limit.
Remote commands work over the system ssh; host-key gating and SFTP are P2 items recorded as the limit.

A real sandbox needs a platform engine the app does not bundle; approvals are the honest local counterpart for now; a sandbox-exec write-clamp was prototyped and refused by this macOS (sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted), so the clamp needs an entitled helper or a VM.
the scratchpad verbs and /scratchpad view have no Playwright coverage in this environment; the loop is implemented and exercised through the turn path.
status chips filter Code sessions in the sidebar; classification itself depends on the Jev session judge and stays unclassified when routing is off.
Commit, Review, and Fix checks draft canned prompts rather than running a skill engine of their own; deeper wiring would ride skills.
comments on the working tree land in the composer un-anchored; per-line anchoring needs a diff-position model the dock does not keep yet.
the compact token block is implemented in CSS and Preferences; visual settings are asserted by eye, not by the suite.
audio playback cannot be asserted headlessly; the chime is an original synthesized asset gated by a Notifications switch.
the hub reads machine facts only inside the desktop app; a browser preview shows a placeholder note.
the default model row patches the same setting the provider screens own; it has no dedicated test.
sending iMessages depends on macOS Automation permission and the Messages app's own state; the bridge reports refusals honestly instead of retrying.
ripgrep ships as a dependency binary; only call-time verification exists and no test asserts match output.
no LaTeX toolchain is bundled; the tool detects Tectonic or TeX at call time and names the install command when absent.
packages load their skills only; MCP servers declared in a package are not started, and the folder watcher has no automated coverage.
the overlay reuses the checked shortcuts list, but the ? key binding itself has no Playwright coverage in this environment.
quoting truncates long messages at 220 characters rather than folding them.
audio playback cannot be asserted headlessly; the ding is an original synthesized asset gated by a setting.
widgets are injected into sandboxed artifact previews; their Shadow DOM rendering needs a browser run the suite cannot make here.
powerSaveBlocker state is observable only in a live app session; wake-from-sleep scheduling needs privileged pmset access and stays unimplemented.
frames depend on the Screen Recording grant and live capture; the recorder keeps only the latest session in temp and asserts nothing headlessly.
the guard reads login-session state through a runtime-compiled Swift helper; refusing mid-typing is asserted by neither the unit checks nor Playwright here.
the admin password prompt and pmset itself live outside the app; the next-occurrence finder is unit-checked and the prompt is the user's chosen path.
live Slack calls need the user's bot token and a real workspace; the tool is gated by the connector toggle and reports Slack's own errors.
live Linear calls need the user's API key and a real workspace; the tool is gated by the connector toggle and reports Linear's own errors.
